routes.label: Use AM-GM midpoint inequalities and continuity to bound the zeros

changes.rationale: Preserve the root-approved derivative-free I28 route rather than broadening h221, whose exact scope covers constants and positive integer powers only. Put C=ln(sqrt(2))/2^(sqrt(2))>0 and F(x)=ln(x)-C*2^x for x>0. No root lies at x<=1; sqrt(2) is a root, F(2)>0 and F(4)<0 give a second beta in (2,4). For distinct positive u,v, AM-GM gives strict midpoint concavity of both ln(x) and -C*2^x, hence F((u+v)/2)>(F(u)+F(v))/2. Induct over bisections for the non-strict dyadic chord inequality and use continuity to extend it to all real weights. If three zeros u<b<v existed, the midpoint of u,v would have positive value; b is that midpoint or a convex combination of it and one endpoint, forcing F(b)>0. Thus exactly two roots occur and 2+sqrt(2)<S<4+sqrt(2)<6, source D. The old derivative-formula gap is genuine for the discarded derivative route but obsolete for this complete AM-GM route; no new derivative or synthesis scope is needed.

changes.rationale: Preserve the approved H route-only midpoint-reflection proof. Bela opens at n/2. After each Bela turn the finite chosen set is invariant under x->n-x. If Jenn chooses a legal x, then for every old z the mirror n-z was old, so |(n-x)-z|=|x-(n-z)|>1. The reply is in [0,n], and |x-(n-x)|=2*|x-n/2|>2 ensures it also avoids Jenn's newest point. Thus Bela can always respond legally and restore symmetry. For k sorted chosen points, consecutive gaps exceed 1, so k-1<span<=n and k<=n; the game must end with Jenn unable to move. Source A follows. The invariant node's actual definition requires preservation under every allowed move and does not itself describe the after-paired-turn strategy. Complete symmetry, distance and inequality components honestly represent the checked route without inventing universal strategy mastery.

routes.label: Locate six roots and prove a degree-six upper bound

changes.rationale: Preserve the approved I28 route-only exhaustive proof. For F(theta)=1-3*sin(theta)+5*cos(3*theta), values at theta=k*pi/3 are strictly positive for even k and strictly negative for odd k. Continuity supplies at least six distinct roots in the intervening open intervals. Put z=cos(theta)+i*sin(theta), nonzero on the unit circle. Polar powers and complex multiplication convert each solution into 5*z^6+3*i*z^4+2*z^3-3*i*z^2+5=0. The factor theorem plus induction bounds distinct zeros of this nonzero polynomial by six; complex-root existence is not needed. The angle parametrization is injective on (0,2*pi], and z=1 is not a zero. Therefore there are exactly six solutions, source D. These complete existing route components do not need an invented universal trigonometric-synthesis node.

routes.label: Classify opposite pairs using even residual paths
Branch on one partner and count residual ladders

changes.rationale: Retain the useful parity, congruence and recursive alternatives but move optional procedures out of universal roles. The exact h232 definition requires a combined addition-and-multiplication procedure, whereas the displayed task requests the number of admissible pairings without prescribing that procedure. Encode acquaintances as the cycle C10 with antipodal edges. Classifying by the number k of antipodal pairs gives counts [2,5,0,5,0,1]: without such pairs the cycle has two alternating matchings; once diameters are selected, every remaining rim path must have even order, and three selected diameters work exactly when the two unselected slots are adjacent on the five-slot cycle. Alternatively fix person 0: opposite partner 5 leaves 5 matchings and either neighbor leaves 4, so 5+2*4=13, source C. The explicit partner-branch route uses both operations and can include h232, while elementary parity and modulo-2 classification are separate OR routes. Use complete route-only mapping, keeping graph modeling in those explicit routes rather than asserting every solver must use a formal graph or combined-counting method.

routes.label: Construct one repeated zero with the required constant terms

changes.rationale: Preserve the already root-approved I28 fundamental-theorem mapping. H(z)=R(z)-P(z)*Q(z) has degree 6 because P*Q has degree 5, so H is nonconstant and the fundamental theorem of algebra guarantees at least one complex zero. To attain one distinct zero take P=z^2+1, Q=z^3+2 and R=P*Q+(z-1)^6. Their degrees are 2,3,6 and constant terms are 1,2,3, and the equation reduces to (z-1)^6=0. Thus N_min=1, source B. The full roots-coefficients scope relates existing roots to coefficients; the remainder-factor scope tests or bounds factors. Neither supplies existence of a complex zero for every nonconstant polynomial. The exact approved fundamental-theorem scope is genuinely needed and retains its separate source-publication gate; preserve the explicit construction as a complete optional route.

records.reason: Retain the original justified power-cycle emphasis; the accepted reviewer's congruence-emphasis variant is also defensible and does not require a union of roles. The numeral's positional expansion is N=2*9^10+7*9^9+6*9^6+5*9+2. Since 9=-1 modulo 5, even powers contribute 1 and odd powers contribute -1, giving 2-7+6-5+2=-2=3 modulo 5, source D. Exact cnm_024 describes numeral systems generally, including binary as a criteria example, so base-nine positional expansion fits. The modular-powers definition explicitly covers justified residue cycles. There is no need to elevate a second equivalent congruence target or demote the directly exercised power-cycle target merely because the reviewer chose another valid emphasis.
